Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, and O is marked on AB as the center of the circle; on the right side there is a vertical chord CD, intersecting AB at H, with C above AB and D below AB; a line segment AC is drawn from A to C, forming ∠CAB. The problem gives CD ⟂ AB at H, ∠A = ∠CAB = 30°, OH = 1.

Reasoning: Connect OC. ∠CAB is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is arc CB, so the corresponding central angle ∠COB = 2∠CAB = 60°. Because O, H, and B are on the same diameter AB, and H is on the right side of O, ray OH is in the same direction as OB, so ∠COH = 60°. Also because CD ⟂ AB, while OH is on AB and HC is on CD, ∠OHC = 90°. Therefore △OHC is a right triangle, with ∠COH = 60°, OH = 1, and OC as the hypotenuse and also the radius of the circle. In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the hypotenuse is 2 times the shorter right side OH, so OC = 2 × OH = 2. The radius of the circle is 2.
